explain.say: Imagine flying round the world in a balloon. Below you, green jungle turns into grassy plains, then sand, then snow. Each big natural region with its own climate, plants and animals is called a biome. Look at the board: let us sort them into four families.

explain.say: Start with the forests. Tropical rainforests, like the Amazon and the Congo, are hot and wet all year. The taiga is a huge cold forest of pine and spruce across Russia and Canada. Deciduous forests, whose trees drop their leaves in autumn, grow in Europe and eastern China. Which would you explore first?

explain.say: Now the grasslands, where there is too little rain for many trees. The savanna of East Africa has lions and zebras. The steppe of Mongolia, the pampas of Argentina and the prairies of North America are cooler grasslands. Can you spot the one with lions?

explain.say: See the deserts? A desert is any place with very little rain, less than 250 millimetres a year. The Sahara is a hot desert, but the Gobi in Mongolia and China is a cold desert, freezing in winter. Were you surprised that a desert can be cold?

explain.say: Last, the cold lands: tundra, where the ground stays frozen and only mosses and small plants grow, and the great ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland. Wonderful sorting! Wow fact: the taiga is the biggest land biome on Earth, wrapping almost all the way round the top of the world.

groups.label: Grasslands
groups.ask: What is the difference between savanna and steppe?

faq.a: A biome is a large natural area with its own kind of climate, plants and animals, like a rainforest or tundra. The same biome can appear on different continents, such as savanna in Africa and Brazil.

faq.q: What is the difference between savanna and steppe?
faq.a: Savanna is tropical grassland, hot all year with wet and dry seasons and scattered trees, like the Serengeti. Steppe is temperate grassland with cold winters and hot summers and almost no trees, like Mongolia.
Yes. A desert is about very little rain, not heat. The Gobi can drop below minus 30 °C in winter, and Antarctica is the largest desert of all.
asks: What is the largest desert in the world?

faq.a: Tundra is a cold, treeless biome in the far north and on high mountains. Below the surface the ground stays frozen all year, called permafrost, and only mosses, lichens and low shrubs grow.
The taiga, or boreal forest, is a huge forest of cone-bearing trees like pine, spruce and larch across Russia, Scandinavia, Canada and Alaska. Winters are long and very cold.
asks: Which is the largest land biome?

facts: A desert is usually defined as a place that gets less than 250 mm of rain a year.
Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth, because so little snow or rain falls there.
The taiga, or boreal forest, is the largest land biome on Earth.

quiz.why: The Gobi gets very little rain and has freezing winters, so it is a cold desert.

wrong.1: Rainforests are hot and wet; the Gobi is dry.
wrong.2: Savanna is tropical grassland, like the Serengeti.

quiz.say: Lions and zebras roam a tropical grassland with scattered trees. Which biome is it?
quiz.show: Tropical grassland with lions and zebras is…
quiz.why: The savanna of East Africa is tropical grassland with scattered trees.

wrong.1: Tundra is cold and treeless, far from lions and zebras.
wrong.2: The taiga is a cold forest of pine and spruce.
